newsitem.title: INDIA: India cotton slide, millers's demand stays low.
newsitem.headline: India cotton slide, millers's demand stays low.

text.p: Indian cotton prices dropped further as demand from millers remained subdued, dealers said.
"Mill buying was slow while higher new crop arrivals prompted fresh offerings by the stockists," they said.
"Millers kept to the sidelines expecting further price erosion while fresh buying by the state-owned agencies including Cotton Corporation of India also remained low," one broker said.
In the spot deals Bengal-deshi slid by 20 rupees to 750/800 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Punjab saw-ginned climbed up 5/10 rupees to 1,375/1,600 rupees per maund.
Gujarat cotton however held steady in a narrow price band.
Gujarat Kalyan (medium staple) was steady at 11,000/11,300 rupees per candy (355.56 kg) while Gujarat Sankar-4 (long-staple) was steady at 16,000/18,000 rupees per candy.
